block-guide:
CORE/BREADCRUMBS (new in WordPress 7.0) A trail of links from Home to the page being viewed: Home / Parent page / This page. WordPress builds the trail itself when the page is shown; the block stores only its settings. Its place is a template or shared header (one block serves every page), or the top of one page. WHAT THE TRAIL SHOWS (built by the server, cannot be typed in) - Page (hierarchical type): Home, its parent pages, the page. - Post / custom record: Home, the post type archive if it has one (posts: the blog page, if set), then the first category or term of the post, with its parent terms, then the post. - Category / tag / term archive: Home, parent terms, the term. Post type, author and date archives, search results ("Search results for: …") and 404 ("Page not found") are covered too. - Page 2 and later adds "Page N". The last item is plain text (aria-current="page"), not a link. The trail follows the real page tree and terms: to change it, change parents or terms. MARKUP (no HTML: the block is a comment only) Never write the
    it renders; colours, fonts, spacing and border go in the comment only. The page shows
    1. …
    . OPTIONS separator: text between items (default "/"); it is drawn by CSS, not written in the list. showHomeItem (true) / showCurrentItem (true): hide the first or the last item. showOnHomePage (false): by default the block shows NOTHING on the front page. prefersTaxonomy (false): for a page-like type that also has taxonomies, use terms, not parents. align: "wide" | "full". PITFALLS An empty space on the home page is the default, not a bug (showOnHomePage). A post with no category or term shows only Home and the post (plus the archive, if any). CHECK Open a child page and a post: the trail lists the real parents / category, each a working link.
